s.g: (computing) To enter information into a device, such as a keyboard or keypad, after it has been done at least once before.
s.x: She had to rekey the security code.

s.g: To modify (a lock or its cylinder) to change which keys will open it.
(social sciences) To change the key or tenor of; to reframe.

rekeying.f: present participle and gerund of rekey

s.g: (computing) The process of entering information into a device again, by means of a keyboard or similar.
(social sciences) The process of changing the key or tenor of something; a reframing.
(intransitive) To be kindled or ignited again.

s.x: After being abroad for a decade, when he came back he rekindled his obsession with cricket.

rekindled.f: simple past and past participle of rekindle

rekindles.f: third-person singular simple present indicative of rekindle

rekindling.f: present participle and gerund of rekindle

s.g: (chiefly philosophy) To know again; to relearn or understand anew.

rekt.f: (Internet slang, video games) Nonstandard spelling of wrecked.
